title: The Deadliest Being on Planet Earth - The Bacteriophage
beats: War for billions of years, trillions killed daily; deadliest entity is the phage.
A phage is a virus, not quite alive; icosahedron head and tail described.
More phages than everything else; billions on your hands; they only kill bacteria.
Phage as cruise missile hunting one family; host specificity.
Step by step infection: attach, syringe, inject, takeover, endolysin burst.
Humans as second deadliest; bacteria were our phages, antibiotics our weapon.
We lost respect, overuse, superbugs, 2050 projection.
Asks 'how could injecting viruses help?'; humans are immune.
Won't bacteria resist? Arms race; resisting phage costs antibiotic resistance.
Patient case, Pseudomonas cured after weeks.
Still experimental; pharma reluctant; trial in 2016; deadliest being could save us.

metrics.misconception: yes: injecting viruses is dangerous; bacteria will just resist, both addressed 4:17-5:30
metrics.ending: Callback to hook 'deadliest being' with caveat, then credits

new_moves.name: voiced-objection
new_moves.what: Narrator interrupts with the viewer's doubt ('Hold on...', 'Wait a minute') and answers it.

new_moves.name: war-metaphor-spine
new_moves.what: One metaphor (war, weapons, monsters) frames the whole video.

theory: One sustained metaphor (war between predators and prey) carries every concept, so new facts slot into a story the learner already holds. The narrator voices the learner's objections at the exact moment they would arise, then answers them.
velocity: Orchestrator: insert scripted 'wait, but...' objection beats at predicted confusion points.
Voice: keep one running metaphor across the session and reuse its vocabulary.
Scene builder: sequential infection animation with step labels.
Evals: check caveats about unfinished science are stated at the end.
quote: Antibiotics are like carpet bombing; phages are guided missiles.
